abstract:
Antimicrobial resistance (AMR) is a major global health threat requiring faster diagnostics than the 24-48 h needed for phenotypic antibiotic-susceptibility testing. Matrix-assisted laser desorption/ionization time-of-flight (MALDI-TOF) mass spectrometry is widely used in clinical microbiology for species identification but does not directly capture AMR phenotypes. Machine learning on MALDI-TOF spectra offers a promising solution, yet existing software remains fragmented across legacy R preprocessing tools and ad hoc Python scripts, lacking standardized workflows, shared application programming interfaces (APIs), and safeguards against train-test leakage.
We present MaldiSuite, a unified Python ecosystem built on a shared data model and a scikit-learn-compatible API. It integrates three packages: MaldiAMRKit (Bruker-native and open-format input/output, standardized composable preprocessing, spectral warping, and temporal drift monitoring); MaldiBatchKit (multi-site batch correction, including MALDI-specific methods, with batch-mixing diagnostics); and MaldiDeepKit (four deep-learning classifiers: multilayer perceptron, one-dimensional convolutional neural network, residual network, and Vision Transformer). All components compose within sklearn.pipeline.Pipeline with leak-safe fit/transform semantics. On the public multi-site Database of Resistance Information on Antimicrobials and MALDI-TOF Mass Spectra (DRIAMS), MaldiSuite achieves an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve of up to 0.92 on the DRIAMS-A Staphylococcus aureus/oxacillin task, and a leakage experiment quantifies the optimistic bias that its leak-safe cross-validation removes.
MaldiSuite is available on PyPI under the MIT licence (pip install maldisuite). Source code: https://github.com/EttoreRocchi/MaldiSuite, https://github.com/EttoreRocchi/MaldiAMRKit, https://github.com/EttoreRocchi/MaldiBatchKit, https://github.com/EttoreRocchi/MaldiDeepKit. The package versions described here and the analysis code of this paper (https://github.com/EttoreRocchi/MaldiSuite-paper), with the pinned environments, are archived at 10.5281/zenodo.24199316.
https://ettorerocchi.github.io/MaldiSuite/.
Supplementary data are available at Bioinformatics online.
